title: Accelerating Federal Permitting of Data Center Infrastructure
key_terms: a facility that requires greater than 100 megawatts (MW) of new load dedicated to AI inference
involving an incremental electric load addition of greater than 100 MW
will utilize federally owned land and resources for the expeditious and orderly development of data centers.
summary: Presidential order directing federal agencies to speed permitting of data center projects and their supporting energy infrastructure. Qualifying projects include those adding more than 100 MW of load, and the order provides for use of federally owned land for data centers.
source_title: The White House — Accelerating Federal Permitting of Data Center Infrastructure

title: Electric Utility Amendments (large-scale electrical loads)
key_terms: This bill creates requirements for providing electrical service to large-scale electrical loads.
the large load customer bears all just and reasonable incremental costs attributable to

This bill takes effect on May 7, 2025.
summary: Creates a new chapter of Utah's public utility code for service to large-scale electrical loads, including a request-and-contract process and Public Service Commission review of large load contracts. The commission approves a contract only if the large load customer bears the incremental costs of its service and existing ratepayers do not.

title: Permits for data centers; emission limits for certain engine-generator sets
key_terms: For any application submitted for a data center on or after July 1, 2026
the Department shall not issue such permit unless the emission limit for each gen-set established by such permit is equal to or less than the emissions achieved by a Tier 4 equivalent gen-set
summary: Adds Va. Code § 10.1-1322.6. For data center air permit applications submitted on or after July 1, 2026, the Department of Environmental Quality may not issue a permit unless each backup generator's emission limit is no higher than a Tier 4 equivalent engine. The department keeps authority to set stricter limits.

title: Electric demand flexibility programs for high energy demand customers
key_terms: has a contracted or measured electric demand of 25 megawatts or greater
each Phase I and Phase II Utility shall file a petition with the Commission for approval of a voluntary demand flexibility program
without unreasonably shifting or imposing any costs of program participation or administration onto other retail electric service customers of the utility
summary: Adds Va. Code § 56-596.7. Defines high energy demand customers as those with 25 MW or more of demand and directs Dominion and Appalachian Power to petition for voluntary demand flexibility programs by January 15, 2027, with cooperatives following by 2029. Any participation incentives must be designed so they do not shift costs to other customers.

title: Data centers; Department of Energy to lead efforts to accelerate use of waste heat
key_terms: shall lead efforts to accelerate the use of waste heat from data centers in the Commonwealth
summary: Directs the Virginia Department of Energy to identify beneficial uses of data center waste heat, recommend ways to connect data centers with heat users, and convene a stakeholder work group. A report goes to the House and Senate commerce committees by September 1, 2026.
source_title: Virginia LIS — HB 323 (2026 Regular Session), Acts of Assembly Chapter 591

title: Certificate of operation for high-load facilities
key_terms: No person shall operate a high-load facility without first having obtained a certificate of operation from the Commission.
will have no material adverse effect upon the rates paid by customers of any regulated public utility in the Commonwealth
summary: Would have required new facilities above a megawatt threshold to obtain a State Corporation Commission certificate of operation, with findings on rate, reliability and environmental effects. Introduced at 25 MW; the House Labor and Commerce substitute raised it to 90 MW and a January 1, 2027 start. Virginia LIS lists the bill as Failed.
